title: Require disaggregated error-rate testing before deploying any risk-scoring algorithm in a high-stakes decision
description: Illustrative reference decision modelled on lessons from the COMPAS recidivism-scoring controversy and the Obermeyer healthcare risk-prediction study. Not a documented decision of any specific organisation.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content, part of the Foundational Twenty.

decision_statement: Before deploying any algorithm that scores individuals' risk (recidivism, illness, default, etc.) to inform a high-stakes decision, the model's error rates (false positive and false negative rates) must be measured and disclosed separately for each protected group, and any proxy variable used as a stand-in for the true outcome of interest must be documented and justified against the risk that it correlates with a protected characteristic.
decision_context: Motivated by two independent, well-documented cases — COMPAS and a widely used US healthcare risk-prediction algorithm — in which risk scores were later found to differ systematically in accuracy across racial groups, in one case traced directly to a proxy variable (healthcare cost) that itself reflected historical inequity.
governing_body: Illustrative example — Algorithmic Risk Assessment Governance Board
alternatives_considered: Rely on a single aggregate accuracy metric rather than disaggregating by group.
Trust a vendor's internal fairness testing without independent disaggregated verification.

citations.title: Machine Bias — There's Software Used Across the Country to Predict Future Criminals. And It's Biased Against Blacks.
Dissecting racial bias in an algorithm used to manage the health of populations
citations.publisher: Science (American Association for the Advancement of Science)
